description: I am participating as a solo developer in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 for the 'Abandoned but not Forgotten' challenge. My objective is to independently analyze the data related to decommissioned or inactive space assets and build a project that fulfills the challenge requirements. I am focused on completing the project successfully on my own.
summary: "Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" is an innovative interactive storytelling and 3D web experience that bridges the gap between cold space telemetry and emotional storytelling. Developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and WebGL via CodePen, it highlights the exact coordinates, historical logs, and final moments of 10 iconic NASA spacecraft, rovers, and landers left behind on the Moon and Mars. The project aims to educate space enthusiasts, preserve off-world heritage, and honor humanity’s first metallic pioneers.
details:
​What does it do or how does it work? "Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" is an immersive digital storytelling and interactive 3D web experience that highlights the historical milestones, telemetry data, and exact coordinates of 10 iconic NASA spacecraft, rovers, landers, and rotorcraft (such as Ingenuity, Opportunity, Viking 1, and the Apollo descent stages) left behind on the Moon and Mars. It merges narrative journalism with interactive 3D web environments to simulate these remote, silent worlds.

What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact? The project transforms dry technical telemetry and open space data into an emotional, human-centric narrative. Its primary goal is to educate students and space enthusiasts about planetary engineering resilience, inspire curiosity for space exploration, and raise awareness regarding the preservation of historic off-world heritage as humanity prepares for future Artemis and Mars missions.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend & Interactive 3D: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and WebGL (developed and hosted via CodePen).
  • Data Sources & Research: Verified open data from NASA Open Data Portals, Planetary Data System (PDS) archives, and NASA mission flight logs.
  • Documentation & Media: Google Docs for comprehensive narrative structuring and video editing tools for our 20-second promotional demonstration.

How is your project creative and what factors did your team consider? Instead of treating retired hardware as mere "space junk," our project frames these machines as eternal monuments to human curiosity. We carefully balanced strict scientific accuracy (exact landing coordinates, sol counts, and mission failure mechanics) with poetic storytelling and 3D visual immersion so audiences can emotionally connect with humanity's footprint across the cosmos.
